title: Platform systems & services: team wiki, playbook, dashboards, runbooks, retrospective, and roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This consolidated team wiki page provides an operational playbook for the Platform Systems & Services team: an inventory of core services, standard how-tos, dashboard and alert conventions, canonical runbooks (on-call and incident), a short retrospective from Q1 2026, and the Q2 2026 roadmap. The goal is to give on-call engineers and new team members a single reference for routine operations, escalation, and planned improvements.

Scope

- Services covered: platform-api, ingress-gateway, k8s-cluster-controller, metrics-ingest, cache-proxy, batch-worker, model-deploy-agent.
- Observability: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), Loki (logs), Tempo (traces).
- Alerting & paging: Alertmanager + PagerDuty integration, Slack incident channels.
- Excluded: Dedicated customer infra (see eng-private-deployments).

Systems & Services Inventory (summary)

1) platform-api
- Purpose: public REST control plane for internal tooling and infra ops.
- SLO: 99.95% availability, P95 latency < 200ms for control operations.
- Owners: service: platform-api, oncall: platform-systems (rotation).

2) ingress-gateway
- Purpose: edge termination, routing, and request shaping for hosted API.
- SLO: P95 request latency < 120ms, healthy upstream rate > 99.9%.
- Notes: rate-limiting middleware (rl-mw) runs as a sidecar.

3) k8s-cluster-controller
- Purpose: manage node pools, autoscale policies, and drain/cordon operations for platform clusters.
- Dependencies: cloud-provisioner, terraform-state store.

4) metrics-ingest
- Purpose: ingest and pre-process Prometheus metrics into long-term TSDB.
- Throughput: ~50k samples/s average; spikes to 250k/s during load tests.

5) cache-proxy
- Purpose: in-memory prefix/KV cache used by runtime GPU host to reduce model token generation cost.

Canonical How-tos (quick references)

- Deploy a minor configuration change (non-breaking):
  1. Create branch: git checkout -b platform-config/<brief-desc>.
  2. Update k8s ConfigMap or helm values in infra repo.
  3. Run unit tests: make test-config
  4. Create PR and request review from owners (codeowners: eng-platform).
  5. Merge when green; monitor canary via Grafana panel "Platform Canary Health" for 15m.

- Rotate TLS certificates for ingress-gateway (short):
  1. Generate cert via internal CA: tools/ca/generate --service ingress-gateway.
  2. Update secret in cluster: kubectl apply -f secrets/ingress-tls.yaml --context prod-cluster.
  3. Trigger rolling restart of ingress pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-gateway -n platform.
  4. Validate: TLS handshake success in 2xx% of connections (check PLT-OV dashboard).

Dashboards & Alerts (conventions)

Dashboard naming and essentials:
- Platform Overview (PLT-OV): high-level SLOs, global 5m latency heatmap, error budget burn.
- Service Detail: one per critical service (PLT-API, PLT-INGRESS, PLT-METRICS).
- Resource Utilization: cluster node CPU/GPU, scheduler backlog.
- Cost telemetry: token throughput, GPU hours, preemptible eviction rate.

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- PLT-API: p95_latency > 350ms for 5m -> page: platform-api-p95-high -> Severity: P1
- Metrics Ingest: samples_dropped_rate > 0.5% for 10m -> page: metrics-ingest-degraded -> Severity: P2
- Cache-proxy: eviction_rate > 500/s for 15m -> notify slack #platform-ops -> Severity: P3

Alert lifecycle rules:
1. Alerts mapped to escalation policies in PagerDuty (P1 -> platform-incident -> SRE lead).
2. Annotate alert with runbook link (Grafana alert message must include runbook URL).
3. If auto-remediation (k8s restart, scaling) fails twice within 15m, escalate to human.

Runbooks (canonical incident steps)

Runbook: platform-api high latency (P1)
- Detection: Grafana alert fires: platform-api-p95-high.
- Triage (5m):
  1. Check PLT-OV for simultaneous cluster-wide signals (ingress, metrics).
  2. Confirm error budget burn and recent deploys: check CI/CD deploy log.
- Mitigation steps (in order):
  1. Rollback most recent control-plane deploy (if one occurred in last 30m).
  2. Increase replica count of platform-api by +30% and watch downstream queue length.
  3. If ingress is saturated, toggle rate-limiter to 80% of current baselines (rl-mw feature flag).
- Post-incident: write incident summary, compute error budget impact, and schedule a 1-hour postmortem in team retro.

Runbook: metrics-ingest backpressure (P2)
1. Validate ingestion lag using prometheus_remote_storage_queue_length.
2. If backlog > 1M samples, scale workers via autoscaling policy or manually scale deployment to N+2.
3. If long-term storage is unresponsive, failover to secondary TSDB (see disaster-recovery doc link).

Retrospective: Q1 2026 (summary)

What went well:
- Completed unified dashboard migration to Grafana 9.x with templated folders; improved on-call time-to-detect by ~20%.
- Implemented autoscale smoothing for batch-worker which reduced thrashing during nightly jobs.

What needs improvement:
- Runbook coverage: two newly-integrated services had incomplete runbooks during incidents. Action: mandate runbook as part of service onboarding (see onboarding checklist).
- Alert noise: duplicate alerts for k8s evictions (fixed by improved relabeling rules, still monitoring).

Action items from retro:
- All new services must have a documented runbook and dashboard before being added to on-call rotation (owner: Liang Zhao, due 2026-03-15).
- Reduce low-severity paging to #platform-notify channel and use a dedup window of 10m (owner: Miguel Torres, due 2026-03-01).

Roadmap (Q2 2026) - priorities and owners

1) Observability uplift (Apr-May)
- Deliverable: standardized dashboard templates, RBAC for Grafana folders, alert ownership assignment.
- Owner: Hannah O'Connor.

2) Runbooks as code (May-Jun)
- Deliverable: store runbooks in repo with linting and automated link generation for Grafana alerts.
- Owner: Asha Patel.

3) Canary & rollout improvements (May-Jun)
- Deliverable: promote canary analysis automation and integrate automatic rollback on regression signals.
- Owner: Platform Release Eng.

4) Cost telemetry (Q2 ongoing)
- Deliverable: per-tenant GPU hours and token-level cost attribution dashboards.
- Owner: infra-finance liaison.

Ownership and contacts

- Team slack: #platform-ops (primary), #platform-notify (low-sev).
- PagerDuty schedules: platform-oncall (primary), platform-incident (incident commanders).
- Primary owners:
  - Platform Systems lead: Miguel Torres (miguel@redwood.com)
  - Observability lead: Hannah O'Connor (hannah@redwood.com)
  - Platform releases: Liang Zhao (liang@redwood.com)

Onboarding checklist for new services

1. Create service page in team wiki with owner, SLOs, SLA impact.
2. Provide Prometheus metrics and at least one Grafana dashboard.
3. Add runbook.md to infra-runbooks repo and link it to Grafana alerts.
4. Validate alert-to-pagerduty mapping and add to on-call rotation only after approval.

Appendices & references

- Templates: /confluence/templates/platform-runbook-template.md
- Grafana folder: grafana/prod/platform (RBAC: team-platform view/edit as appropriate).
- Oncall playbook (short): /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-playbook-2025
- Service onboarding checklist: /confluence/eng-platform/service-onboarding-checklist

If anything is missing or unclear, open a PR against this document in the eng-platform wiki repo or ping the platform lead in Slack.
